name: Vertical turbine pump line-shaft bearings
author: Sample data
desc: Water-lubricated line-shaft bearings in a 6-stage vertical turbine pump supplying a municipal reservoir.
problem: Bronze bearings seized after every dry start-up and wore the stainless shaft sleeves, with a rebuild needed about every 14 months.
solution: Hilube bushes with four straight flush grooves, fitted with a light interference fit, replaced the bronze bushes in all six bearing positions.
proof: No seizures in 30 months of service. Measured bush wear under 0.2 mm and shaft sleeve wear negligible at the last inspection.
summary: Pump bearings that survive dry starts and last more than twice as long between rebuilds.
env: Clean river water, intermittent dry starts

name: Stern tube bearing for a coastal workboat
author: Sample data
desc: Water-lubricated stern tube bearings on the 55 mm propeller shaft of a 14 m coastal workboat.
problem: Lignum vitae bearings wore quickly in silty water and the vessel had to be hauled out every 18 months to re-bush the stern tube.
solution: Vesconite stern tube bearings with water-cooling grooves, sized with the running clearance for water lubrication.
proof: Three years in service with bearing clearance still within tolerance at the second haul-out, and no unplanned stops.
summary: Marine bearings that stay in tolerance between dry-docks, even in silty water.

name: Excavator boom pin bushes
author: Sample data
desc: Boom and stick pin bushes on a 120 tonne hydraulic excavator working in an iron ore pit.
problem: Steel-backed bronze bushes needed greasing every shift, consumed grease, and the pins were being scored by abrasive dust.
solution: Hilube bushes with a lubricant-retaining groove pattern. The greasing interval was extended from every shift to every 250 hours.
proof: Grease consumption fell by about 60% and no pin scoring was found at the 2,000 hour inspection.
summary: Pin bushes that cut grease use and protect the pins in dusty, high-load digging.

name: Hydro turbine wicket gate bushes
author: Sample data
desc: Upper and lower wicket gate stem bushes in a 4.5 MW Francis turbine in a small hydro scheme.
problem: Greased bronze bushes leaked grease into the water and the maintenance outage for re-greasing was costly.
solution: Grease-free Hilube bushes replaced the bronze bushes and the grease system was removed from the gate stems.
proof: Five seasons without regreasing, gate torque unchanged, and no oil or grease discharged to the river.
summary: Grease-free gate bushes for hydro turbines, with lower maintenance and a cleaner river.

name: Sluice gate guide strips
author: Sample data
desc: Wear strips on the guides of a 2.4 m wide sluice gate on an irrigation canal.
problem: Phosphor bronze guides corroded and the gate stuck at full opening during the irrigation season.
solution: Vesconite guide strips screwed into the gate frame with counter-sunk fasteners.
proof: The gate has operated smoothly for 4 seasons and the lifting force fell by about 30%.
summary: Corrosion-free guide strips that stop sluice gates sticking.

name: Mine winder clutch bushes
author: Sample data
desc: Flexible bushes in the drum clutch of a deep-level mine winder.
problem: Rubber-based bushes cracked from fatigue and needed replacement more than once a year.
solution: Vescoflex elastomer bushes, sized for a slight press fit, replaced the rubber bushes.
proof: Tested at 5 MPa for 2.5 million cycles with no visible degradation and still in service after 14 months.
summary: Tough flexible bushes that outlast rubber in a demanding clutch application.

name: Rail wagon bogie bolster liners
author: Sample data
desc: Wear liners in the centre bowl of freight wagon bogie bolsters.
problem: Steel-on-steel contact caused bolster wear, wagons ran skew and wheel flanges wore out early.
solution: Hilube cup and flat liners that give low stick-slip so the wagons return to alignment.
proof: Flange wear dropped noticeably over two years and the bolster bowls were no longer being re-welded.
summary: Low-friction liners that protect the bogie and extend wheel life.
load: Static load about 200 kN per bogie

name: Planter chain tensioner bushes
author: Sample data
desc: Chain tensioner and seed drive bushes on a 12-row maize planter.
problem: Nylon bushes wore out each season in dusty fields and caused chain slack and uneven seed spacing.
solution: Vesconite bushes with the same envelope as the nylon parts, machined from rod.
proof: The same bushes ran two full seasons with no measurable slack in the chain drive.
summary: Bushes that keep planter drives accurate through dusty seasons.

name: Forklift mast roller bushes
author: Sample data
desc: Roller bushes in the lift mast of electric counterbalance forklifts working two shifts.
problem: Greased bronze bushes attracted dirt and dripped grease onto pallets and the warehouse floor.
solution: Hilube bushes that run dry and keep the mast rollers turning freely.
proof: No lubrication needed for 18 months and the clean-up costs from grease drips stopped.
summary: Grease-free bushes that keep warehouse masts clean and quiet.

name: Forestry log loader pin bushes
author: Sample data
desc: Crane pin bushes on a truck-mounted log loader.
problem: Greased pin joints collected bark and grit, wore the pins and needed regular rebuilds.
solution: Vesconite pin bushes replaced the steel sleeves, with the greasing interval stretched to monthly.
proof: Pin and bush wear stayed under 0.3 mm after 3,000 operating hours.
summary: Pin bushes that tolerate bark, grit and rough handling.
